nameStory: The winged thecacera gets its name from the wing-like projections that extend from its body, giving it an almost ethereal, flying appearance as it glides through the water. The scientific name 'pennigera' literally means 'wing-bearing' in Latin, perfectly capturing this sea slug's most distinctive feature.
description: The winged thecacera is a type of nudibranch, which is a shell-less sea slug that breathes through external gills. These translucent marine creatures are among the ocean's most beautiful invertebrates, with delicate wing-like extensions called cerata projecting from their soft bodies. They're relatively small animals that you might encounter while tidepooling or diving in New England's coastal waters. As nudibranchs, they're actually gastropods - related to snails and slugs - but have evolved to live without shells.

idTips.label: Wing-like projections
idTips.description: Look for distinctive translucent, flattened extensions that project from the body like delicate wings or fins, giving the animal its characteristic flying appearance

idTips.label: Translucent body
idTips.description: The body appears glassy and semi-transparent, often allowing you to see internal structures and digestive contents through the skin

idTips.label: External gills
idTips.description: Feathery or branched gill structures visible on the outside of the body, usually appearing as delicate, tree-like projections

idTips.label: Soft, gelatinous texture
idTips.description: If gently touched, feels soft and jelly-like with no hard shell or rigid structures - handle very carefully as they're extremely delicate

idTips.label: Tentacle-like rhinophores
idTips.description: Two sensory tentacles at the head end that may be rolled or club-shaped, used for detecting chemicals and food in the water

habitat: Winged thecaceras are found in New England's cold Atlantic waters, typically in rocky intertidal zones and subtidal areas. They prefer areas with good water circulation where they can find their prey, often hiding among seaweeds, under rocks, or in crevices during low tide. You're most likely to spot them in tide pools or while snorkeling in rocky coastal areas from Maine to Massachusetts.

seasonality.spring: May begin appearing in warmer tide pools as water temperatures rise. Look carefully in protected rocky areas during very low tides.
seasonality.summer: Most active and visible during summer months when water temperatures are warmest. Best viewing during calm, clear days at low tide.
seasonality.fall: Still present but may be less active as temperatures cool. Continue checking tide pools during exceptionally low tides.
seasonality.winter: Rarely seen due to cold water temperatures and harsh conditions. Most likely retreated to deeper, more stable waters.

funFact: Despite being related to garden slugs, winged thecaceras are actually fierce predators that hunt other sea slugs - they're like tiny underwater wolves that can completely devour prey larger than themselves by turning their stomachs inside out!
confusionNotes: With only 2 recorded observations in New England, winged thecaceras might be confused with other translucent nudibranchs, but the distinctive wing-like projections set them apart from the more common frilly or spike-covered species. Remember: if it looks like it's 'flying' underwater with translucent wings, you've likely found this rare beauty.
contextualKnowledge: The term 'nudibranch' means 'naked gill' in Latin, referring to their external breathing structures. Many people are surprised to learn that these colorful sea creatures are actually mollusks - the same group that includes clams, oysters, and garden snails - but they've evolved far beyond their shelled relatives.
compareHints: Since there are no other Thecacera species in our dataset for New England, compare the winged thecacera to other nudibranchs in the Polyceridae family by looking for its distinctive wing-like extensions. Most other nudibranchs in New England waters have either frilly cerata (finger-like projections) or completely different body shapes, making the winged appearance quite unique.
